primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Susceptibility mutations, most commonly in RYR1, make the skeletal-muscle ryanodine receptor open excessively in response to triggering anesthetics, causing uncontrolled sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium release, rigidity, hypermetabolism, acidosis, and hyperthermia.
vignette: Shortly after induction of general anesthesia with a volatile agent and succinylcholine, a 24-year-old man develops generalized muscle rigidity, rapidly rising end-tidal CO2, tachycardia, acidosis, and hyperthermia.
lead: Which intracellular event is most directly responsible for this syndrome?
correct: Excessive release of calcium from the skeletal-muscle sarcoplasmic reticulum
distractors: Reduced calcium entry through cardiac L-type channels
Failure of acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction
Inhibition of troponin C binding to calcium
Depletion of ATP from red blood cells
distractor_notes: Cardiac L-type calcium-channel reduction does not explain anesthetic-triggered skeletal-muscle rigidity and hypermetabolism.
Presynaptic acetylcholine failure causes flaccid paralysis, not rigidity and heat generation.
Inability of troponin C to bind calcium would impair contraction rather than cause sustained contraction.
Red blood cells lack the contractile apparatus responsible for this syndrome.
key_expl: Malignant hyperthermia is driven by uncontrolled skeletal-muscle calcium release, usually through abnormal RYR1 channels after trigger exposure.
objective: Explain malignant hyperthermia through dysregulated RYR1-mediated calcium release.

sources.title: Malignant hyperthermia
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes RYR1/CACNA1S susceptibility and excessive calcium release causing rigidity, heat, and acidosis.

sources.title: RYR1 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes ryanodine receptor 1, skeletal-muscle calcium release, and malignant-hyperthermia variants that open too easily and close too slowly.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Reactive arthritis is sterile inflammatory arthritis that occurs after certain genitourinary or gastrointestinal infections; the joint itself is not infected.
vignette: A 26-year-old man develops asymmetric knee and ankle arthritis, conjunctivitis, and dysuria 3 weeks after an episode of urethritis. Arthrocentesis shows inflammatory fluid but bacterial culture is negative.
lead: Why can the inflamed joints remain culture-negative despite the recent infection?
correct: The arthritis is a sterile postinfectious inflammatory response rather than direct bacterial invasion of the joint
distractors: Bacteria are present but cannot grow in any standard culture medium
The joint contains only deposited urate crystals
The infection directly destroys synovium while remaining confined inside neutrophils
The arthritis results from age-related cartilage wear after infection
distractor_notes: Reactive arthritis is not explained by viable unculturable bacteria directly occupying the joint.
Urate crystals cause gout, not the classic post-urethritis arthritis/conjunctivitis syndrome.
Direct microbial invasion of the joint would represent septic arthritis rather than reactive arthritis.
Degenerative cartilage wear causes osteoarthritis and does not explain the acute postinfectious inflammatory syndrome.
key_expl: Reactive arthritis is triggered by an infection elsewhere in the body, but the affected joint is not directly infected; therefore synovial cultures can remain negative.
objective: Explain culture-negative arthritis after genitourinary or gastrointestinal infection as sterile reactive arthritis.

sources.title: Reactive arthritis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes sterile arthritis following genitourinary or gastrointestinal infection, often with eye and urinary manifestations.

sources.title: Infectious Arthritis
sources.support: MedlinePlus distinguishes infectious joint disease and provides context for postinfectious/reactive arthritis.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Hematogenous or direct microbial invasion of a joint causes acute intense inflammatory monoarthritis; prompt recognition and drainage/antimicrobial therapy are needed to limit cartilage destruction.
vignette: A 67-year-old woman with diabetes develops fever and a rapidly swollen, exquisitely painful knee. She cannot tolerate passive motion. Arthrocentesis yields purulent, neutrophil-predominant synovial fluid.
distractor_notes: Crystal arthritis can produce intense inflammation but must be distinguished by crystal analysis and does not explain purulent fluid plus systemic infection as well.
CPPD can cause acute monoarthritis but is crystal-mediated rather than infection-driven.
Reactive arthritis is usually sterile and occurs after an infection elsewhere.
Osteoarthritis is a chronic degenerative process, not febrile purulent monoarthritis.
key_expl: Fever, severe acute monoarthritis, pain with passive motion, and purulent neutrophil-rich synovial fluid strongly indicate septic arthritis.
objective: Recognize septic arthritis as an urgent infectious cause of acute monoarthritis.
clues: fever and acutely painful swollen joint

sources.title: Septic arthritis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes acute fever, severe monoarticular pain/swelling, synovial aspiration, culture, and microbial joint infection.

sources.title: Infectious Arthritis
sources.support: MedlinePlus identifies septic arthritis as infectious inflammation of a joint.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Chondrosarcoma is a malignant bone tumor composed of cartilage-producing cancer cells, occurring most often in adults and commonly involving the pelvis, proximal femur, or shoulder region.
vignette: A 58-year-old man has months of deep pelvic pain. Imaging shows a destructive lobulated pelvic bone mass with chondroid matrix calcifications. Biopsy shows malignant cells producing cartilage.
distractor_notes: Osteosarcoma produces malignant osteoid and is more common in adolescents or has different age/location patterns in secondary disease.
Ewing sarcoma usually affects children and adolescents and is a small round blue-cell tumor.
Giant cell tumor is typically an epiphyseal lesion with osteoclast-like giant cells, not malignant cartilage production.
Multiple myeloma produces plasma-cell neoplasia and lytic lesions rather than a cartilage-forming pelvic mass.
key_expl: An adult with a cartilage-producing malignant bone tumor, especially in the pelvis, has chondrosarcoma.
objective: Recognize chondrosarcoma from age, location, and malignant cartilage production.

sources.title: Chondrosarcoma
sources.support: NCI describes chondrosarcoma as cartilage-producing bone cancer, often affecting adults and common in pelvis/long bones.

sources.title: Chondrosarcoma - NCI Dictionary
sources.support: NCI defines chondrosarcoma as cancer forming in bone cartilage, often in the pelvis, shoulder, ribs, or long bones.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Fibromyalgia is a chronic widespread pain syndrome associated with altered central processing of pain, fatigue, nonrestorative sleep, and cognitive symptoms without inflammatory joint destruction.
vignette: A 42-year-old woman has 8 months of widespread aching pain, fatigue, nonrestorative sleep, and difficulty concentrating. Examination shows diffuse soft-tissue tenderness but no synovitis; ESR and CK are normal.
distractor_notes: Polymyositis causes objective proximal weakness and often elevated muscle enzymes rather than pain-dominant diffuse tenderness.
RA causes inflammatory synovitis with joint swelling and prolonged stiffness.
SLE may cause arthralgia but generally has additional systemic/serologic features and does not define this chronic pain-processing syndrome.
Hypothyroid myopathy can cause weakness and myalgias but would be supported by thyroid abnormalities.
key_expl: Chronic widespread pain with fatigue, sleep disturbance, cognitive symptoms, normal inflammatory testing, and no synovitis is characteristic of fibromyalgia.
objective: Recognize fibromyalgia as a chronic widespread pain-processing disorder rather than inflammatory muscle or joint disease.
clues: fatigue/nonrestorative sleep with normal inflammatory studies

sources.title: Fibromyalgia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes chronic widespread pain, fatigue, sleep problems, cognitive symptoms, and altered pain processing.

sources.title: Fibromyalgia - Medical Encyclopedia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes long-term widespread pain with fatigue, sleep and concentration problems and abnormal central pain processing.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Autoimmune attack on lacrimal and salivary glands reduces tear and saliva production, causing keratoconjunctival and oral dryness with possible systemic autoimmune manifestations.
vignette: A 49-year-old woman has gritty painful eyes, dry mouth, recurrent dental caries, and difficulty swallowing dry food. Examination shows reduced tear and salivary production.
lead: Which tissue is the primary autoimmune target in this disorder?
correct: Exocrine glands that produce tears and saliva
distractor_notes: Zona glomerulosa destruction causes mineralocorticoid deficiency, not sicca symptoms.
Beta-cell destruction causes type 1 diabetes mellitus.
ACh receptor autoimmunity causes myasthenia gravis, not dry eyes/mouth from gland destruction.
Anti-GBM disease causes pulmonary-renal disease rather than lacrimal/salivary dysfunction.
key_expl: Sjögren disease primarily targets moisture-producing exocrine glands, especially lacrimal and salivary glands.
objective: Link sicca symptoms to autoimmune destruction of lacrimal and salivary glands.

sources.title: Sjögren's Disease
sources.support: NIAMS describes autoimmune attack on moisture-producing glands with dry eyes and mouth.

sources.title: Sjogren's Syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes autoimmune damage to tear and salivary glands causing ocular and oral dryness.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Sarcoptes scabiei mites burrow into the superficial skin; hypersensitivity to mites and their products causes intense nocturnal pruritus, papules, and serpiginous burrows in characteristic locations.
vignette: A college student develops severe itching that is worst at night. Examination shows small papules and thin serpiginous burrows in the finger webs and wrists. Her roommate has similar symptoms.
distractor_notes: Tinea corporis produces annular scaly plaques rather than burrows with nocturnal pruritus among close contacts.
Atopic dermatitis is chronic eczematous disease and does not spread by close contact.
Herpes zoster causes painful grouped vesicles in a dermatomal distribution.
Contact dermatitis follows exposure to a sensitizing substance and does not produce transmissible mite burrows.
key_expl: Nocturnal pruritus, finger-web burrows, and spread among close contacts are classic for scabies.
objective: Recognize scabies from its nocturnal pruritus, burrows, distribution, and contagious contact pattern.

sources.title: About Scabies
sources.support: CDC describes Sarcoptes infestation, intense itching, papular rash, burrows, and spread by prolonged skin contact.

sources.title: Symptoms of Scabies
sources.support: CDC describes nocturnal pruritus and characteristic involvement of finger webs, wrists, and other sites.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Dermatophyte infection of keratinized skin causes pruritic annular scaly plaques with an active raised border and relative central clearing.
vignette: A wrestler develops several enlarging pruritic circular plaques on the trunk. Each lesion has a scaly raised erythematous edge with relative central clearing.
distractor_notes: Nummular eczema produces coin-shaped eczematous plaques but lacks the classic advancing ring border with central clearing.
Psoriasis produces well-demarcated plaques with scale, often on extensor surfaces, without the typical annular advancing edge.
Erythema multiforme produces target lesions rather than scaly annular dermatophyte plaques.
Impetigo produces superficial erosions with honey-colored crust.
key_expl: An itchy annular scaly rash with a raised advancing border and central clearing is tinea corporis (ringworm).
objective: Recognize tinea corporis by its characteristic annular dermatophyte rash.
clues: scaly raised edge with central clearing

sources.title: Symptoms of Ringworm
sources.support: CDC describes tinea corporis as a red itchy ring-shaped rash with scale, raised border, and possible central clearing.

sources.title: Treatment of Ringworm
sources.support: CDC identifies ringworm as a fungal skin infection treated with antifungal therapy.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Varicella-zoster virus remains latent after primary infection and can reactivate along a sensory nerve distribution, causing a painful unilateral vesicular dermatomal eruption.
vignette: A 67-year-old man develops burning pain over the right chest followed 2 days later by grouped vesicles in a narrow band from the back to the sternum. The rash does not cross the midline.
distractors: Reactivation of herpes simplex virus in the trigeminal ganglion
Dermatophyte invasion of the stratum corneum
distractor_notes: Primary VZV infection produces diffuse chickenpox rather than a unilateral dermatomal eruption.
HSV reactivation may cause oral/genital or focal lesions but this thoracic dermatomal syndrome is classic for zoster.
Dermatophytes cause annular scaly lesions, not grouped painful vesicles in a dermatome.
Immune-complex vasculitis causes palpable purpura rather than dermatomal vesicles.
key_expl: Shingles is caused by reactivation of latent VZV, producing painful vesicles in a unilateral sensory dermatome.
objective: Explain herpes zoster as reactivation of latent VZV along sensory pathways.

sources.title: About Shingles
sources.support: CDC states that shingles occurs when latent varicella-zoster virus reactivates after prior chickenpox.

sources.title: Shingles Symptoms and Complications
sources.support: CDC describes painful unilateral stripe-like vesicular rash and preceding pain/tingling.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Rising pressure within a noncompliant fascial compartment impairs local perfusion and compresses muscles and nerves; urgent fasciotomy prevents irreversible ischemic injury.
vignette: A 29-year-old man has a tibial fracture placed in a cast. Several hours later he has rapidly worsening leg pain out of proportion to the injury, severe pain with passive toe extension, paresthesias, and a tense swollen compartment.
lead: Which mechanism best explains the progression of this condition?
correct: Increased intracompartmental pressure compromises tissue blood flow
distractors: Arterial vasodilation increases capillary oxygen delivery
Venous valve incompetence causes chronic edema
distractor_notes: Vasodilation would not explain escalating pressure within a closed fascial space.
Demyelinating neuropathy causes weakness/sensory symptoms but not a tense postfracture compartment.
Chronic venous insufficiency develops gradually and does not cause acute pain with passive stretch after fracture.
Urate crystals cause gouty synovitis, not closed-compartment ischemia.
key_expl: Fascia cannot expand sufficiently; rising pressure compresses vessels and nerves and can block blood flow, causing muscle and nerve ischemia.
objective: Recognize acute compartment syndrome and explain tissue injury through pressure-mediated perfusion compromise.
clues: pain out of proportion with passive stretch

sources.title: Compartment syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes increased pressure within a fascial compartment, impaired blood flow, muscle/nerve damage, and need for urgent fasciotomy.

sources.title: Bruise - Compartment syndrome discussion
sources.support: MedlinePlus notes that compartment syndrome is extreme pressure buildup that can reduce blood and oxygen supply to tissues.
